curriculum.title: Grade 10
curriculum.description: Ontario Grade 10 Principles of Mathematics, Academic (MPM2D) for YRDSB learners: practice with varied question styles and guided exploration. Activities support practice, not certification of mastery.

children.title: Mathematical processes
children.description: Use problem solving, reasoning, reflecting, tools, connecting, representing and communicating in every strand.
children.example: Explain how you checked a solution.

children.title: Quadratic relations of the form y = ax² + bx + c
QR1 · Basic properties of quadratic relations
Collect and model quadratic data
children.description: Collect data that follow a quadratic relation and draw a curve of best fit.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Parabolas and second differences
children.description: Show that a quadratic relation graphs as a parabola with constant second differences.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Key features of a parabola
children.description: Identify the axis of symmetry, vertex, y-intercept, zeros and maximum or minimum.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Quadratic and exponential relations
children.description: Compare y = x² and y = 2ˣ and give meaning to negative and zero exponents.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Effects of a, h and k
children.description: Identify how translations, reflections and stretches change y = x².
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Roles of a, h and k
children.description: Explain the roles of a, h and k in y = a(x − h)² + k.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Sketch by transformations
children.description: Sketch y = a(x − h)² + k by transforming y = x².
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Equation from a graph
children.description: Determine the equation y = a(x − h)² + k of a parabola from its graph.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Expand and simplify
children.description: Expand and simplify second-degree polynomial expressions.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Factor polynomials
children.description: Factor common factors, trinomials and differences of squares.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Factors, zeros and intercepts
children.description: Connect factors of a quadratic to the zeros and x-intercepts of its graph.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Real and non-real roots
children.description: Interpret real and non-real roots using graphs and the discriminant.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Complete the square
children.description: Express y = ax² + bx + c in the form y = a(x − h)² + k.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Sketch from y = ax² + bx + c
children.description: Graph a quadratic relation by intercepts, symmetry or completing the square.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: The quadratic formula
children.description: Explore the development of the quadratic formula and use it.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Solve quadratic equations
children.description: Solve quadratic equations with real roots by factoring, the formula or graphing.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Zeros and extreme values
children.description: Find zeros and maximum or minimum values from a graph or equation.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Quadratic models in context
children.description: Solve problems from realistic situations modelled by quadratic relations.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: AG1 · Using linear systems to solve problems
Solve linear systems
children.description: Solve systems of two linear equations by substitution and elimination.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Linear systems in context
children.description: Solve problems from realistic situations using linear systems.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: AG2 · Properties of lines and line segments
Midpoint of a segment
children.description: Develop and use the formula for the midpoint of a segment.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Length of a segment
children.description: Develop and use the formula for the length of a segment.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: The circle x² + y² = r²
children.description: Develop the equation of a circle centred at the origin.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Radius and equation of a circle
children.description: Find the radius from an equation, write the equation from a radius, and sketch the circle.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Slope, length and midpoint problems
children.description: Solve problems involving the slope, length and midpoint of a segment.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Investigate figure properties
children.description: Investigate characteristics of figures such as medians and similar figures on right triangles.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Verify properties with coordinates
children.description: Verify perpendicular lines, equal sides and other properties using analytic geometry.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Multi-step verification
children.description: Plan and carry out a multi-step strategy to verify a property of a figure.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Properties of similar triangles
children.description: Verify the properties of similar triangles.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Similarity and congruence
children.description: Describe and compare similarity and congruence.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Similar triangles in realistic situations
children.description: Solve problems with similar triangles such as shadows and scale models.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Sine, cosine and tangent
children.description: Define the primary trigonometric ratios from similar right triangles.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Solve right triangles
children.description: Find side lengths and angles using the primary ratios and the Pythagorean theorem.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Right-triangle applications
children.description: Solve real-life problems with the primary ratios.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: The sine law
children.description: Explore the sine law in acute triangles and use it.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: The cosine law
children.description: Explore the cosine law in acute triangles and use it.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Solve acute triangles
children.description: Find sides and angles of acute triangles with the sine and cosine laws.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

children.title: Acute-triangle problems
children.description: Solve problems about acute triangles in realistic situations.
children.example: Try the pictured or story question. Explain your method, then refresh to explore another style.

suggestedSequence: Parabolas, transformations, factoring, completing the square, the quadratic formula and models.
Linear systems, midpoints, distance, circles at the origin and verifying figures with coordinates.
Similar triangles, sine, cosine and tangent, and the sine and cosine laws in acute triangles.
